title: Deltafin: 2.8T Kimi K3 from Four SSDs on a MacBook - Layer Streaming as a Local Inference Lever (Michael Kerkhoff, Context Studios blog, published 23 Sep 2026; benchmarks dated 8 Sep 2026)
id_read: blog HTML at .../deltafin-2-8t-kimi-k3-from-four-ssds-on-a-macbook-layer-streaming (catalog URL is truncated)
setup: MacBook Pro M5 Max 128 GB, four NVMe SSDs (bandwidth not stated), Kimi K3 2.8T MoE, 1.45 TB expert weights, 16 experts/token, argonautlabsai/deltafin fork of gavamedia/deltafin; optional small drafter model; every value from a single cold run; baseline only the upstream repo on M1 Max (0.2901 tok/s; 0.68 on the 17-token prompt)

numbers.where: table; prefill re-reads each layer's experts 8 times, fix not built

catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: 6.3 min

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: author names prefill as main limit
catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: 'the true design limit'; cause = 8x re-read of each layer's experts
author is Michael Kerkhoff, Founder (named byline); first-pass note 'author unnamed' is wrong
I fetched only the -layer-streaming URL; truncated URL not re-tested

why: Same idea family (stream experts from NVMe, batch 1, no expert skipped) but 128 GB RAM = 9 % hot fraction, 4 SSDs, Apple unified memory, 16 experts of a 2.8T model. Not CPU-only 8-32 GB. Prefill figure measures a naive (non layer-major) prefill. One data point that matters: real SSD scaling is sub-linear (1 to 2 drives gives 1.40x, not 2x), so an ideal-2x stripe assumption should be treated as optimistic.
quality_loss: none claimed (all experts used, drafter verified); no quality benchmark reported
ablation: drafter on/off; SSD count 1-4 (percentages only). No cache vs layout vs prefetch ablation.
limitations: single cold run per setting; prefill 8x re-read, fix unbuilt; author recommends short prompts
contradicts_our_findings: No contradiction; sub-linear SSD scaling is a caution against our 2 NVMe = 2x stripe arithmetic (pubtech/C.md 2.39 to 4.78 tok/s), measured in a different regime (cache-heavy, 16 reads in parallel per layer, slowest read dictates).

catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: only token-importance scoring (raw Q.K dot products) on FPGA

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: notes SSD bandwidth remains bottleneck even with in-storage compute
catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: paper argues the CSD removes the host PCIe bottleneck via P2P; the bandwidth limit cited is host-SSD KV transfer. The 3.2 GB/s device figure is the supporting fact
v2 (latest) states ~3.2 GB/s; 4 GB/s is v1
same in v1 and v2

why: KV scoring, not weights; GPU 4090 host; batch 8. Useful fact: a real SmartSSD reads NAND at ~3.2 GB/s internally, the same as one laptop NVMe (3.1 GB/s measured in our work), so in-storage compute buys no extra weight bandwidth per drive.
quality_loss: accuracy comparable to full cache and baselines at 10-80 % retention (Fig 11, graphs only)
limitations: authors note FPGA resource limits and selective algorithm simplification (softmax removed); setup inconsistent (RTX 3080 32 GB in intro)
